extracted.intended_audience: Institutions of higher education, scholars, academic leaders, and humanities-focused organizations seeking Mellon Foundation support
extracted.subtask_short: applying to Mellon Higher Learning grants
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance describing who Mellon’s Higher Learning programs support and the kinds of projects and partnerships the Foundation funds in the humanities. Useful for prospective institutional applicants, scholars, and humanities organizations preparing to engage with Mellon.

rubrics_metrics.name: Colleges and universities (eligible recipients)
rubrics_metrics.description: Colleges and universities exploring new directions in humanistic study in a range of learning environments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page explicitly lists 'Colleges and universities' as recipients and emphasizes exploration of new directions in humanistic study across varied learning settings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scholars and academic leaders (eligible recipients)
rubrics_metrics.description: Scholars and academic leaders working to deepen our understanding of American history and culture, advance new methods for scholarly interpretation, and elevate underrepresented perspectives in academia.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlights individual scholars and leaders as grantees when their work addresses American history/culture, methodological innovation, or elevating underrepresented perspectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Humanities-focused organizations (eligible recipients)
rubrics_metrics.description: Humanities-focused organizations committed to expanding public understanding and appreciation of the liberal arts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organizations outside universities that are committed to public-facing humanities work are named as supported recipients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Programmatic activities funded
rubrics_metrics.description: Mellon funds academic research, curricular development, extracurricular programming, internships, and community partnerships.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Foundation broadens opportunities in the humanities through these modes of work; proposals aligning with these activity types are within the program’s scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority content areas and aims
rubrics_metrics.description: Projects should address crucial societal issues, produce new knowledge, and promote the spirit of learning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasis on work that engages societal concerns, generates scholarship or new insights, and fosters learning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on American history, culture, and underrepresented perspectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Support for work that deepens understanding of the United States, its cultures, and people, and that elevates underrepresented perspectives in scholarship and curricula.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page calls out American history and culture and the elevation of underrepresented perspectives as central concerns for funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional inclusion and types (targeted institutions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Includes institutions such as rural universities, tribal colleges, HBCUs, and more.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mellon explicitly names a range of institutional types, signaling attention to geographically and historically underserved or mission-driven institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding beyond colleges and universities
rubrics_metrics.description: The Foundation also funds humanities projects beyond colleges and universities that deepen understanding of the United States and help ensure the breadth of stories told and studied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-academic humanities projects that expand public knowledge and diversify narratives are within funding scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partnership orientation
rubrics_metrics.description: We partner with institutions that are expanding the definition of education and learning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preference for collaborative work with institutions innovating in how education and learning are conceived and delivered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invitation-driven grantmaking process
rubrics_metrics.description: Staff seek out and get to know innovative organizations, scholars, and creators before inviting them to submit a proposal; most Mellon grants are made through these invitations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The program is largely proactive and relationship-driven—applicants should note that unsolicited proposals may be uncommon and that cultivating relationships with program staff or being known to staff increases likelihood of invitation.
